title: Python SSE adapter + async collector with bounded-queue backpressure and graceful migration
creator: Ava Chen
description: Context: Customers increasingly use newline-delimited SSE and chunked HTTP streams for chat completions. The current Python SDK surface exposes low-level callback and event-handler primitives that are hard to compose and don't integrate well with asyncio backpressure patterns. This ticket introduces a reusable SSE adapter and an async collector pattern backed by a bounded asyncio.Queue to provide predictable memory usage, simple resume semantics, and a migration path from callback-style handlers to async iterators/context-managers. Goals: (1) reliably parse delimited SSE / newline-delimited JSON events including partial-chunk boundaries, (2) provide a safe default bounded queue for backpressure with configurable size and drop/fail policies, (3) expose a lightweight async context-manager wrapper that yields an async iterator over complete events and automatic checkpointing hooks, and (4) document migration examples and add tests/benchmarks.
acceptance_criteria: SSE adapter correctly parses SSE-like streams ("data: " lines and NDJSON) across chunk boundaries and emits full JSON events to consumers
Default Python API: `with sdk.chat.stream(... ) as stream: async for event in stream: ...` works with bounded queue (default size 128) and does not OOM when producer is faster than consumer
Backpressure policies supported: block (await until queue space), drop_oldest, drop_newest, fail_with_exception — configurable per-call
Adapter exposes optional low-level callback shim for existing customers for backward compatibility
Comprehensive unit tests for chunk boundary parsing, queue policies, and reconnect/backoff semantics
Benchmarks showing <5% median latency regression for typical 1k token responses compared to unbounded callback path when queue size is 128
Docs and migration guide with at least two examples: (a) callback-style to async iterator migration, (b) integrating telemetry hooks (latency/counter)
design_decisions: Use an asyncio.Queue as the canonical in-memory buffer. Default size 128 chosen from internal benchmarks balancing memory vs throughput.
Expose backpressure_policy enum: 'block', 'drop_oldest', 'drop_newest', 'fail' to cover common patterns without surprising defaults. Default = 'block' to preserve correctness.

Parse stream bytes incrementally. Maintain a small buffer and use line-based splitting but handle partial JSON spanning multiple chunks using a simple accumulator and attempt incremental json.loads when a newline is encountered.
Provide an async context-manager wrapper that manages queue lifecycle and graceful shutdown (drain on completion, propagate last error to consumers).
Keep a low-level callback adapter API: on_event(payload: bytes) -> None for backwards compatibility and for advanced users.
Reconnect/backoff strategy implemented at the transport layer: exponential backoff starting at 500ms, cap 8s, full-jitter. Expose hooks to override for dedicated/private customers.
implementation_notes: Module: redwood.sdk.streaming.sse_adapter with classes: SSEClientTransport, AsyncEventCollector
SSEClientTransport reads from httpx.AsyncClient.stream("GET", ...) and yields raw bytes; uses chunk_size 8192 to match common server chunking patterns
AsyncEventCollector runs a background task that parses bytes into complete event payloads and puts them into an asyncio.Queue according to policy
Checkpoint API: collector.checkpoint(token: str) stores last-seen event id in memory and emits it to the consumer via event.metadata; persistent checkpointing integrated later via Optimize hooks
Expose simple helper: from_bytes_to_event(payload_bytes) -> dict | str to centralize parsing and error handling
Add metrics: counter.stream_events_received, counter.stream_events_dropped, histogram.queue_length, gauge.queue_capacity to the SDK's telemetry facade
Add configuration knobs: queue_size (int), backpressure_policy (str), transport_timeout_ms (int), reconnect_backoff_ms (base,int,cap)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: JSON fragmentation across chunks may cause parser to attempt partial loads and raise exceptions. Mitigation: only attempt json.loads on newline-terminated candidate strings; fall back to returning raw text event and attach parse_error metadata.

Risk: Blocking default may lead to head-of-line blocking in sync wrappers. Mitigation: provide non-blocking helper and ensure docs explain default trade-offs; consider timeouts for blocking put operations
Risk: Behavioral differences from existing callback API could break customers. Mitigation: provide shim adapter and a migration guide with examples and tests to validate parity for common patterns
Risk: Background task leaks on cancellation. Mitigation: rigorous shutdown logic in context-manager and unit tests with asyncio.CancelledError scenarios
test_plan: Unit tests: chunked_stream_parsing.py tests for 1-5 chunk fragmentation cases including unicode boundaries
Property tests: randomized chunk boundary generator that asserts event reconstruction equals original payloads
Policy tests: ensure drop_oldest and drop_newest behave as documented under producer flood
Integration tests: run end-to-end against a small local SSE test server that emits controlled delays and reconnects
Load test: synthetic producer that emits 20K small events/sec to verify queue pressure and metric emission
CI: Add flakiness guard with retries on integration tests that depend on timing, and run benchmarks in a reproducible runner
rollout_plan: Feature branch -> internal SDK alpha build -> dogfood in Redwood Console's chat simulator for 1 week
Collect telemetry: queue_length, events_dropped, reconnect_count from dogfood apps
Iterate on defaults based on dogfood results (queue_size 128 may become 256 for certain workloads)
Beta release: opt-in behind environment flag 'SDK_STREAMING_V2' for external beta testers
GA: Set as default after 4 weeks of stable beta and feedback, publish migration guide and changelog
